subject: Spectra-7B elevated 5xx / timeout behavior — incident & recovery updates
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@skyforge.ai>
To: hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@skyforge.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Spectra-7B /api/generate timeouts and 5xxs (production)

Hi Hiro / Redwood team,

We started seeing an uptick in 524 gateway timeouts and intermittent 500/503 responses when calling your Spectra-7B endpoint from our production service around 08:50 PDT. Error rates jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% and correlated with higher tail latency (p95 -> ~4200ms). This is impacting our chat product — some user sessions are dropping mid-conversation.

We've attached a short capture of request traces and a gzipped set of logs (logs_rpm-20270401.zip). Happy to provide any other traces you need. Can you confirm if you're aware of a degradation and ETA to restore normal operation?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Senior SRE, SkyForge

--
Attachment: logs_rpm-20270401.zip (application/zip, 4.2MB)

From: hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@skyforge.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spectra-7B /api/generate timeouts and 5xxs (production)

Hi Elena — thanks for the report and the logs. We're seeing the same signal in our telemetry: a surge of long-running requests pinned to a subset of Spectra-7B serving nodes in us-west-2. Initial triage indicates KV cache growth and GC pressure on a particular kernel path that handles attention cache eviction.

Immediate actions we've taken (live):
- Scaled the Spectra-7B pool +30% to shift traffic off suspect nodes.
- Forced prefix/KV cache flush on the affected hosts.
- Rolled back a recent kernel micro-optimization introduced in last week's deploy (patch id: rw-kern-20270329-c) on canary hosts.

We're collecting dtrace snippets and a core sample; attaching a small snippet (dtrace-snippet.txt) to help correlate. We'll follow up with an hourly status update and a recovery ETA.

Short-term ETA: if rate normalizes with pool scaling and cache flush, we expect progressive recovery within 45-90 minutes. If not, next step will be to fully rollback the micro-optimization across the affected fleet.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you posted and prioritize your traffic routing until this is resolved.

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: dtrace-snippet.txt (text/plain, 12KB)

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai

Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@skyforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spectra-7B /api/generate timeouts and 5xxs (production) — mitigation update

Quick update from infra/serving: after the cache flush and scaling we saw a drop in error rate to ~1.1% and p95 latency returned to ~1100ms for most customers, but SkyForge's sessions still see occasional spikes when traffic lands on two legacy nodes. We're in the process of cordoning those hosts and re-draining.

Action items in-flight:
- Cordoning and re-provisioning two legacy nodes (expected 18 minutes to re-drain).
- Global routing rule: pin SkyForge to the newer pool to avoid fallback to legacy nodes (applied).
- Roll forward a temporary kernel hotfix to stabilize eviction earlier than full rollback (candidate build rw-kern-20270401-hotfix).

Elena — can you confirm whether pinning to the newer pool reduced your error spikes? If you still see issues after 10m, we'll initiate a full rollback.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Spectra-7B incident summary and next steps (postmortem follow-up)

Hi Elena — closing the thread with a short post-incident summary and concrete next steps. Thank you and your team for the quick traces; they were instrumental in identifying the root cause.

What happened (summary):
- On 2027-04-01 ~08:45 PDT a subset of Spectra-7B hosts started exhibiting elevated request tail latency leading to 524 and higher 5xx rates.
- Root cause: an eviction logic regression in a kernel micro-optimization (rw-kern-20270329-c) which caused KV cache to grow under certain multi-tenant prefix patterns. The growth increased GC and CPU contention on some older kernels, causing timeouts under bursty workload.

What we did (timeline highlights):
- 09:00: scaled Spectra-7B capacity +30% and forced prefix/KV cache flush on affected nodes.
- 09:10: cordoned two legacy nodes and re-routed SkyForge to the newer pool; error rate dropped significantly for affected sessions.
- 09:35: deployed rw-kern-20270401-hotfix across the canary pool; followed by staged rollback of rw-kern-20270329-c where necessary.
- 11:15: full fleet stabilization and monitoring showed error rates back to baseline (<=0.3% for Spectra-7B) and latency trending to normal.

Impact: SkyForge observed intermittent session drops for ~1.5 hours during the incident window; we estimate customer-visible failures impacted ~0.6% of requests for your tenant during that window.

Follow-up commitments (owner / ETA):
- Full RCA doc and timeline posted: https://drive.redwood.example.com/Shared/Spectra7B/postmortem-20270403.md (Hiro, 2027-04-03).
- Backport durable mitigation to older kernel images and orchestrate a canary rollout (Markus, 2027-04-10).
- Improve per-tenant routing safeguards to avoid fallback to legacy nodes when tail latency is detected (Grace, 2027-04-17).
- Offer SkyForge 1 week of enhanced remediation credits and a 1:1 postmortem review (Hiro, coordinate by 2027-04-05).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the technical postmortem and answer questions. Would next Tuesday (Apr 6) at 11:00 PDT work for you?

Again, apologies for the disruption. We appreciate the partnership and will prioritize stabilization work to reduce recurrence risk.

Best regards,
Hiro Tanaka
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
